title: GE Aerospace Commits $100K to Embry-Riddle to Support Transitioning Service Members
summary: Donation marking Embry-Riddle’s 100th anniversary will help service members complete the Aviation Maintenance Technology SkillBridge programDAYTONA BEACH, Florida – November 18
body_markdown:
*Donation marking Embry-Riddle’s 100th anniversary will help service members complete the Aviation Maintenance Technology SkillBridge program*


**DAYTONA BEACH, Florida – November 18, 2026 –** To mark Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University’s 100th anniversary, GE Aerospace Chairman and CEO H. Lawrence Culp, Jr., announced a $100,000 donation during the university’s Presidential Speaker Series to support its Aviation Maintenance Technology SkillBridge program, helping transitioning service members complete their training.


“Embry-Riddle and GE Aerospace trace our roots to Ohio, and we both believe the industry’s future depends on a skilled workforce,” **said H. Lawrence Culp, Jr.** “Veterans and service members are essential to this effort, bringing leadership, technical skills, and commitment to a mission. As Embry-Riddle celebrates 100 years, we’re committed to supporting service members as they transition into aerospace careers.”


The donation will help cover tuition and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) testing expenses for service members in the program. Offered through Embry-Riddle’s Worldwide Campus, the nine-week program combines aviation maintenance training with career preparation and employer engagement, and has more than 1,000 graduates to date.


“We are incredibly grateful to GE Aerospace and Larry Culp for this powerful investment in our service members and the Aviation Maintenance Technology SkillBridge program,” **said Embry-Riddle President P. Barry Butler, Ph.D.** “Helping service members transition to civilian careers is central to the missions of both Embry-Riddle and GE Aerospace. We are honored that this generous gift will prepare more service members to enter roles critical to the aerospace industry from Day One.”


This donation builds on GE Aerospace’s ongoing efforts to support workforce training opportunities for service members and veterans. Since 2024, GE Aerospace and the GE Aerospace Foundation have donated more than $2 million toward veterans’ skills training, job placement, and career readiness, including through the Foundation’s flagship workforce program,[Lifting Futures](https://www.liftingfutures.org/) .


To learn more about how GE Aerospace is helping build the talent pipeline for aerospace and advanced manufacturing, visit[geaerospace.com/workforce](https://geaerospace.com/workforce) .


**About GE Aerospace**
GE Aerospace is a global aerospace propulsion, services, and systems leader with an installed base of approximately 50,000 commercial and 30,000 military aircraft engines. With a global team of approximately 57,000 employees building on more than a century of innovation and learning, GE Aerospace is committed to inventing the future of flight, lifting people up, and bringing them home safely. Learn more at[www.geaerospace.com](https://www.geaerospace.com/)
